name: dev-document
description: Floe developer/document guest. Extends the basic template with git and command-line developer tools (wget, jq, rsync, tree, tmux), the network diagnostics the approved template lists (curl, iproute2, iputils-ping, traceroute, bind9-dnsutils, netcat-openbsd, mtr-tiny, tcpdump), the C/C++ build chain (build-essential, gcc, g++, make, pkg-config, python3-dev) so wheels without a riscv64 build can compile, pandas and the Debian-provided document Python stack (Pillow, lxml, openpyxl, python-docx, PyMuPDF), plus the pinned PyPI wheels Debian trixie does not ship (python-pptx, pdfplumber with its exact pdfminer.six/pypdfium2 pins). The wheel dependency closure that Debian provides (Pillow>=9.1, lxml, XlsxWriter, typing-extensions, charset-normalizer, cryptography) is installed from apt, so the offline --no-index wheel install pulls only the four pinned files. Apt Python packages (including python3-numpy and python3-pandas) live at /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages and are visible to the per-environment shared venv only through --system-site-packages: the language package UI reports them as inherited/read-only (writable=false); packages pip installs into the venv are the writable layer. Size measured from the trixie riscv64 indices: the added dependency closure is about 120 packages / 839 MB installed versus the basic image (toolchain ~639 MB, dev tools ~102 MB, document stack ~107 MB, pandas ~39 MB); the actual installed size is recorded by the image build's package inventory.
